unit.why: A single anecdote about the holy rabbi (R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev, per the book's section) who, while in Hungary, pretends to be a shochet in order to teach a careless butcher a lesson.
unit.boundary_note: Division ends with a section heading ('שיחות ומאמרים מתוקים ממנו הקדוש...') that belongs to the following sayings section, not to the story.

stories.start_quote: יסופר בשמו שפ"א בא באונגארין אצל קצב
stories.summary_en: In Hungary a butcher who does not recognize the tsaddik asks him to slaughter a beast. The tsaddik pretends to be a shochet and asks for a loan of twenty roubles. When the butcher refuses to lend money to a stranger, the tsaddik points out that he was ready to trust that same stranger with kashrut, which is a far graver matter. The butcher repents.
